A.ud_core_note: 12 clusters x 64 cores, from triton driver get_device_properties(0).device_model=3; torch.cuda.get_device_properties is stubbed and reports 8 MP, which is wrong
A.device_code_backend_note: Only Triton compiles to executable device code on this stack. nvcc/PTX cannot run on P800; clang-written device code does not link; the XHPC/xpucc SDK is absent from the container; the XPU ELF loader needs torch's in-process runtime state, which a bare C++ host cannot reproduce (see docs/device-stack.md).

P.radix_note: v0 baseline is radix-2; M5 adds radix-4 as a second processing unit on the same baseline flow (compare arithmetic cost against radix-2). radix-8 and others remain unexplored.

dit_stage_kernel.note: First DIT stage optionally reads X[bit_reverse(i)] and X[bit_reverse(i)+n], folding the input permutation into stage 0

dif_stage_kernel.note: Last DIF stage optionally writes through bit-reversal, folding the output permutation into the final stage

stage_fusion.level_note: M0 baseline: one global-memory round trip per stage
stage_fusion.fused_tiles_note: M1 candidate axis: compile-time local micro-FFT tile. tile=1 is the M0 baseline (no fusion); tile=64 fuses the first log2(64)=6 block-local stages into one kernel. Stages n < tile are block-local (pairs (i,i+n) stay inside a tile-aligned block), so the fused kernel needs no cross-program barrier.
stage_fusion.gather_scatter_note: The tested Triton 3.0.0 XPU lowering rejects the tensor-subscript gather Xt[idx_tensor] (ValueError: Did you forget to add @triton.jit?) but ACCEPTS pointer-form gather tl.load(ptr + idx_tensor); canaries: tests/test_fft.py::test_tensor_subscript_gather_blocked / test_pointer_form_gather_lowers. M1 uses only pointer tl.load/tl.store.

batch_expansion.note: M4 data-space/time expansion over the (B, N) batch axis. 'spread' maps batch to grid axis 1 (Ud=B, flow batch-spread); 'folded' splits the batch out of a flat pair-space grid (Td=B, flow batch-folded). Both consume B in dit/dif_stage_batch_kernel and keep the M0 stage count (log2(N) launches); batch=1 degenerates to the baseline. The batch axis is a workload axis, not an assumed speedup (plan sections 6/7). batch=256 joined the published axis with issue #8 (stress domain N=1024,B=256): a workload axis entry measured by the semantic-matrix confirmation sessions, still no assumed speedup; the lowering contract and selector validation read this same list.

register_matrix.note: M2 register-resident local matrix (flow_realization=matrix-resident, processing_unit=dense-dot-fft64). The tile stage group is a dense (BLOCK x BLOCK) linear map through 4x tl.dot; one program owns `rows` consecutive tile-blocks, the group crosses device memory exactly once (one load, one store) and all stage intermediates stay in registers feeding the implicit dot. tiles/rows are powers of two; runtime still requires the tile to divide N (runner clamps eff_tile). This list is the single published M2 search space: the cost model's bounded search, the focus harness's enumerated m2_t* variants, the benchmark keys, the lowering contract and the selector table validation all read it from here (issue #3 fix: one shared candidate description -- the tile=128 rows in {4,8,16} family that won the batch focus shapes is part of the space, not an off-config default).

grouped_boundary.note: M3 execution-group boundary tail (flow_realization=grouped-boundary, processing_unit=composite-linear-map). Tail stages half-span n >= tile are partitioned into execution groups of up to `glog` consecutive stages with period n0<<g <= maxp (see src/xpu/matrices.py tail_groups); a group is one pointer-form linear map so only group boundaries cross global memory. `cells` is how many BLOCK windows one group-kernel program owns. `rows` matches the runner default (tile-blocks per program); bench does not expose it as a CLI flag.

L.planar_note: Split real/imag float32 pairs. The Triton XPU backend has no complex64 argument type (KeyError: 'complex64' in type_canonicalisation_dict), so interleaved complex is not an option for kernel arguments.

G.twiddle_layout: planar cos/sin tables of exp(-2*pi*i*idx/N) for idx in [0, N/2); stage reads W[j*M] with M = N/(2n)
G.twiddle_source: global-memory tables built once per size by twiddle_tables(); recomputed per stage by the (unused) on-chip prototype

F.dft_matrix_note: No hardware matrix-unit path; the P800 matrix engine is not reachable from a Triton kernel on this toolchain. The M2 register_matrix flow is different: it lowers through Triton's tl.dot builtin (compiler-generated code), which does work - see P.register_matrix.

H.warp_size_note: Triton reports warp_size=1 and warpSize=1 for this backend
